'''Wolfgang Wienand''' (born 22 February 1972) is a business executive and former Olympic [[fencing|fencer]]. Since 2024, he has been [[chief executive officer]] (CEO) of [[Lonza Group]], Swiss-based company in the contract development and manufacturing organization ([[contract development and manufacturing organization|CDMO]]) industry. He previously was chief scientific officer and then CEO at [[Siegfried AG|Siegfried]]. He competed in the individual and team [[foil (fencing)|foil]] events at the [[1996 Summer Olympics|1996]] and [[2000 Summer Olympics]]. 

==Education==
Wienand studied chemistry at the [[Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms University]] in [[Bonn]] and received a PhD in [[organic chemistry|Organic]] and [[bioorganic chemistry|Bioorganic Chemistry]] from the [[University of Cologne]] in [[Germany]].<ref>[https://www.uni-due.de/akschmuck/alumni.shtml Research Working Group of Prof. Dr. Carsten Schmuck]</ref> His studies have been supported by academic and PhD scholarships of the [[Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes]], Germany's national academic merit foundation, as well as the Kekulé PhD scholarship of the Fonds des VCI (Verband der Chemischen Industrie), Germany’s national chemical-industrial association.<ref>[https://www.vci.de/services/publikationen/vci-spotlight.jsp About Verband der Chemischen Industrie]</ref> He later completed an Executive Master of Science in Finance at [[École des hautes études commerciales de Paris | HEC Paris]] in France. 

==Professional career==
Wienand joined [[Lonza Group]] in July 2024 as CEO.<ref>[https://www.lonza.com/news/2024-07-01-07-00 Lonza Welcomes New Group Chief Executive Officer Wolfgang Wienand] Official statement from Lonza, 02 April 2024</ref> He has led the strategic transformation of [[Lonza Group|Lonza]] into a pure-play [[contract development and manufacturing organization|CDMO]], including the divestment of the Capsules & Health Ingredients business and the introduction of the company's streamlined operating model under the One [[Lonza Group|Lonza]] strategy.<ref>[https://www.lonza.com/news/2024-12-12-06-25 Lonza Investor Update 2024 Outlines Strategy, New Organizational Structure and Guidance] Official statement from Lonza, 12 December 2024</ref>

Since 2023, he has been a Non-Executive Director on the Board of Mettler-Toledo International.<ref>[https://investor.mt.com/governance/board-of-directors/person-details/default.aspx?ItemId=34a22602-f532-4add-8507-2b837b3fe0b9 Person Details: Dr. Wolfgang Wienand, Chief Executive Officer, Lonza Group Ltd]</ref> 

Wienand was CEO  of [[Siegfried AG|Siegfried]] from 2019 to 2024.<ref>[https://www.siegfried.ch/changes-in-siegfrieds-management-team/ Changes in Siegfried’s Management Team] Official statement from Siegfried, 02 April 2024</ref> Earlier, he was Chief Scientific Officer and then Chief Strategy Officer in Siegfried's executive leadership team.<ref>[https://www.siegfried.ch/changes-in-siegfrieds-management-team/ Changes in Siegfried’s Management Team] Official statement from Siegfried 02 April 2024</ref> Prior to joining Siegfried in 2010, he held a series of positions with increasing seniority at [[Evonik Industries AG]].      

==Sports career==
As a [[foil (fencing)|foil]] [[fencing|fencer]], Wienand was a long-standing member of the national fencing team of Germany and the German Olympic teams of [[Atlanta]] 1996 and [[Sydney]] 2000.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20200417222524/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/wi/wolfgang-wienand-1.html Olympic Results of Wolfgang Wienand]</ref> He won the World Youth Championships in 1989 in [[Lisbon]]. He finished in 4th place at the [[1996 Summer Olympics]] in Atlanta and won the bronze medal at the [[1999 World Fencing Championships]] in [[Seoul]].<ref>[https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/22345 Wolfgang Wienand Biographical Information]</ref> He came second in the individual competition at the [[1998 European Fencing Championships]] in [[Plovdiv]], where he also won the European championship with Germany's men's foil team,<ref>[https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/22345 Wolfgang Wienand Biographical Information]</ref> as well as winning the World Cup Series in 1997. Wienand was ranked number one in the world and won seven World Cups and several German National Championships.

Since 1991, his coach was Frank-Eberhard Höltje, later the German national coach for the men's [[foil (fencing)|foil]], who had previously served as national coach of the [[German Democratic Republic|GDR]] men's junior [[foil (fencing)|foil]] team and competed as a [[sabre]] [[fencing|fencer]] at the [[1980 Summer Olympics]] in Moscow. Previously Wienand was coached by Manfred Kaspar, former German national coach for [[epee]] and sports director of the German national fencing association. His home club is the Olympic Fencing Club (OFC) Bonn.

Wienand was a leading figure in the German national team. He finished his career in sports after the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] to complete his PhD and to start over with his professional career in the chemical-pharmaceutical industry.

==Awards==
* Germany's fencer of the year 1996
* Germany's junior fencer of the year 1989
